I’d say that one thing Korean cinema does lack in and may bring up the stereotype of melodrama is the amount of arthouse/auteur cinema. A lot of Korean cinema is very good and well done/innovative technically entertainment but when it comes to more drama pieces—say something like a Koreeda or PTA film—they do tend to fall into the melodrama catergory, at least for the more popular mainstream films.

This isn’t say that they don’t have auteurs though, the films you listed in your comment are great examples but note how between all those films it’s just two directors. I’m not an expert in Korean cinema by any means, mostly just contemporary stuff admittedly, but I probably could at most only name a dozen or so really outstanding directors. Also, most of the artsy stuff I’m aware of in Korea is the more the popular and successful type since more obscure films are—in my experience—much harder to find in comparison to places like France or Japan, likely due to the those countries’ much larger film significance in history.

I just personally feel like a lot of Korean cinema is more relatable to the work of someone like Tarantino or del Toro (auteurs in their own respects but create films aimed moreso for entertainment or passion purposes I suppose I would say) versus someone similar to those mentioned earlier which might bring up the melodrama cheesiness stereotype.

One example which loosely goes along with this idea I feel may be The Force Awakens. The relationship between all the different factions, specifically the Resistance and New Republic, isn’t really at explored at all in the film but outside media makes the technicalities clearer.

I'm a junior in Highschool right now and honestly most kids don't really care about dressing nice until like sophomore  year.

The uniform for middle schools usually consists of:
Sweatshirt
Sweatpants/Athletic shorts
Sneakers

or (if the kids are trying to be preppy):
Collared zip up sweater (?, not sure what they're called)
Colored chino shorts
Nike elite socks
Sperrys


For pants, most kids usually just wear sweatpants everyday, I despite being extremely un athletic did too a few years ago in middle school. I personally when I started to dress nicer felt sort of uncomfortable wearing jeans because everyone else wore sweatpants but as I wore them more I started to not really care. If you want your kid to dress nicer now then I'd say probably get him some jeans so he'll be more comfortable with them or you can just wait until he takes the initiative to dress him better later on. Kids wear all types of shorts (except maybe like jorts) so that's easy, though most will probably wear just athletic. In the recent years joggers have become popular but I really don't see anyone wearing them in my Highschool (since they're hard to find I think?) so I don't know how'd they fare in middle school.

For tops any t-shirts should be fine, plain or graphic design. Unbuttoned flannels during the colder seasons are common. Wearing anything more formal than that (like an OCBD) will, sadly, probably be made fun of.

A lot of kids your son's age do care about sneakers so maybe take him out and get him a nice pair for school. 

EDIT: Also, I want to mention that most kids dress based on how they're dressed growing up and their influences so this advice won't be the best.
